questions.question: Which is NOT a primary aim of exercise therapy?

options.C: Replacing the need for medical diagnosis

questions.explanation: Exercise therapy improves mobility, strength, endurance, coordination and function.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which starting position gives the greatest stability for an exercise?
questions.explanation: Lying positions give the largest base of support and lowest centre of gravity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A movement is performed in a gravity-eliminated plane when it occurs:
questions.explanation: E.g. hip abduction in supine, or elbow flexion in sitting with the arm supported on a table (for grade 2).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A therapist helps a patient to flex the knee when the quadriceps are weak, using a sling suspension. This is a:
questions.explanation: The patient contributes effort; the sling reduces friction/gravity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The main purpose of relaxed passive movement is to:

options.D: Maintain joint range, soft tissue extensibility and circulation when active movement is not possible

questions.explanation: Forced passive movement is used to stretch adhesions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Forced passive movements are usually performed:

options.B: Under anaesthesia or with great care to stretch shortened tissue

questions.explanation: They may cause tissue damage and are not used in myositis ossificans.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: An advantage of manual resistance over mechanical resistance is that:

options.D: Resistance can be varied through the range according to the muscle's strength curve

questions.explanation: The therapist adjusts for pain, fatigue and the changing mechanical advantage.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Isometric strength gains are specific to the joint angle at which the muscle is trained, extending approximately:

options.B: 10° either side of the training angle

questions.explanation: Therefore multiple-angle isometrics are used.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A recommended isometric hold for strengthening is about:
questions.explanation: Hettinger and Müller: a single 6-second contraction at two-thirds of maximum daily.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The McQueen regimen of progressive resisting exercise uses:

options.C: A maximal load for each session, increased as tolerated, aiming for a given number of repetitions

questions.explanation: It differs from DeLorme and Oxford regimens in its method of determining the load.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Eccentric training is useful in the rehabilitation of:
questions.explanation: Loaded lengthening stimulates collagen remodelling.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Codman's (pendulum) exercises are used to:

options.A: Gently mobilise the shoulder with the arm hanging relaxed, using gravity and body sway

questions.explanation: Early rehabilitation after shoulder surgery or in a painful stiff shoulder.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Finger-ladder (wall climbing) exercises are primarily for increasing:
questions.explanation: Overhead pulleys and wall ladders improve range in adhesive capsulitis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Neural gliding (flossing) exercises aim to:

options.C: Restore the mobility of a nerve relative to its surrounding tissue

questions.explanation: Used in carpal tunnel and sciatic nerve entrapment.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The contract–relax technique involves:

options.A: A contraction of the antagonist only
options.D: An isometric (or concentric) contraction of the tight muscle followed by relaxation and passive stretch

questions.explanation: Used to increase muscle length via autogenic inhibition.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the agonist-contract technique of PNF stretching, the stretch is gained by:

options.D: Actively contracting the antagonist of the tight muscle (reciprocal inhibition)

questions.explanation: Sometimes called contract–relax–antagonist contract (CRAC).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A fast, forceful stretch of a muscle is generally avoided because it:

options.B: Excites the muscle spindle, causing a reflex contraction that resists the stretch

questions.explanation: A slow, sustained stretch is preferred.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Thomas position is used to stretch the:
questions.explanation: The lumbar spine is flattened against the couch to avoid substitution.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: To stretch the gastrocnemius the knee should be kept:
questions.explanation: Soleus is stretched with the knee flexed.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In treating an established joint contracture, a low-load prolonged stretch is more effective than:
questions.explanation: Creep produces a plastic deformation with less injury risk.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A wobble (balance) board is mainly used to train:
questions.explanation: Used after ankle sprains and in ACL rehabilitation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which statement about proprioceptive training is correct?

options.C: It aims to restore joint position sense and neuromuscular control after injury

questions.explanation: Progress from stable to unstable surfaces and from eyes open to closed.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The ‘core’ stability muscles include:

options.C: Transversus abdominis, multifidus, pelvic floor and diaphragm

questions.explanation: The local stabilisers control segmental stability of the lumbar spine.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A Swiss (gym) ball is useful in exercise therapy because it:

options.A: Provides an unstable surface that challenges balance and trunk muscles

questions.explanation: Used for core strengthening and posture training.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Williams' flexion exercises are traditionally prescribed for:

options.B: Lumbar spinal stenosis and facet syndrome (to open the foramina)

questions.explanation: They aim to flex the lumbar spine and strengthen the abdominals and glutei.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A ‘back school’ programme principally provides:

options.C: Education on posture, lifting, ergonomics and exercise for low back pain

questions.explanation: Group educational and exercise sessions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Pilates exercise emphasises:

options.D: Core control, breathing and controlled movement

questions.explanation: Used for low back pain and posture.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the cognitive (early) stage of motor learning, the learner:

options.C: Needs high attention, makes many errors and benefits from clear instructions and demonstration

questions.explanation: Stages (Fitts and Posner): cognitive, associative, autonomous.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Knowledge of results (KR) in motor learning is:

options.B: Information about the movement pattern itself
options.C: Information about the outcome of the movement relative to the goal

questions.explanation: Knowledge of performance (KP) refers to the movement pattern.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Cooper 12-minute run/walk test estimates:
questions.explanation: Distance covered in 12 minutes is converted to VO₂ max.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A moderate-intensity aerobic exercise is about:
questions.explanation: Light 57–63%, vigorous 77–95% HRmax (ACSM).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A 100-metre sprint relies mainly on the:
questions.explanation: Glycolysis supports efforts lasting 30 seconds to 2 minutes; aerobic metabolism beyond that.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: During prolonged low-intensity exercise, the predominant fuel source is:

options.C: Fat (free fatty acids) with some carbohydrate

questions.explanation: Carbohydrate use increases with intensity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A feature of overtraining syndrome is:

options.A: Persistent fatigue, reduced performance and raised resting heart rate

questions.explanation: Needs reduced training and rest.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: During prolonged exercise in the heat, dehydration causes:

options.D: Reduced performance and an increased risk of heat illness

questions.explanation: Fluid replacement is essential.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The most serious form of heat illness is:

options.C: Heat stroke (core temperature > 40 °C with CNS dysfunction)

questions.explanation: Medical emergency; cool rapidly.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Circuit training involves:

options.B: Moving between a series of exercise stations with short rests
options.C: Doing one exercise for an hour

questions.explanation: It can improve strength endurance and cardiovascular fitness.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In older adults, which type of exercise is MOST important for preventing falls?
questions.explanation: Tai chi and the Otago exercise programme are effective.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Rolling from supine to side-lying in a patient with hemiplegia is facilitated by:

options.B: Pulling on the bed rail with the affected arm
options.D: Flexion of the hip and knee of the leg to be rolled over and the arm reaching across

questions.explanation: Rolling trains trunk rotation and prepares for transfers.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Rising from a chair requires the centre of gravity to move:

options.D: Forward over the feet before the hips lift

questions.explanation: Forward trunk lean and foot placement under the knees assist.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A therapist should assist a patient in a bed-to-chair transfer by:

options.A: Using a correct lifting technique, a gait belt and explaining each step
options.B: Lifting alone with a flexed back
options.D: Pulling the patient by the arms

questions.explanation: Wheelchair brakes must be locked.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: For a stand-pivot transfer the wheelchair should be placed at an angle of about:

options.A: 30–45° to the bed on the patient's stronger side

questions.explanation: Move toward the strong side.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A sliding board transfer is used mainly for patients who:

options.A: Cannot stand or bear weight through the legs but have good upper limb strength

questions.explanation: Used in paraplegia and lower limb amputees.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Wheelchair push-ups are performed to:

options.A: Relieve pressure on the ischial tuberosities

questions.explanation: Should be done every 15–30 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Early gait training for a patient after a lower limb fracture usually begins in the:

options.A: Parallel bars with the weight-bearing instructions

questions.explanation: Progress to walking frame, crutches, stick.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A tilt table is used to:

options.C: Gradually accustom patients to the upright position and prevent orthostatic hypotension

questions.explanation: Angles are increased in steps with vital sign monitoring.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Standing frames in paediatric rehabilitation are used to:

options.B: Provide weight bearing, bone loading and reduce contractures

questions.explanation: Standing for 1–2 hours a day improves hip development.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The best position to sleep in for a patient with a flaccid hemiplegic arm is:

options.A: In a sling at all times
options.B: On the affected shoulder with the arm under the body
options.C: Supine or side-lying with the arm supported on pillows and the shoulder protracted
options.D: With the arm hanging off the bed

questions.explanation: Prevent shoulder subluxation and pain.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which measure protects the heels of a bedridden patient from pressure damage?

options.A: Placing the foot against a footboard
options.C: Pillows under the calves so the heels are free of the mattress

questions.explanation: Heel offloading boots can also be used.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
